label: Length-3 sequences: first copy step after <DEL> (outputting token 1); weakly on a leading u/v
explanation: Two clauses, both about absolute position. (1) Main mode, about 80% of activation mass and every top activation: in L=3 sequences it fires at step t=4, the first copy step after <DEL>, where the input is orig(0) fed back and the output is orig(1). It fires on 100% of such steps and reaches the max (about 0.22), and the identity of the input token makes little difference. (2) Weak mode, about 16% of mass at about 0.03-0.06: step t=0 when the first token is u or v, for any L. Residual misses (about 10% of mass, small magnitudes) all fall at t=5: L=4 sequences at recall_idx 1 and L=3 sequences at recall_idx 2, which fire only occasionally and weakly. It never fires on the delimiter step, at t=1-3, or at t>=6, so it is silent for longer sequences except at t=0 and t=5.

issues: The t=0 u/v clause is weak in magnitude (16% of mass) but covers about 59% of active steps by count (test recall 0.59 on its own), so calling it 'weak' is true by mass and understates it by frequency.

'Identity of the input token makes little difference' at L=3 t=4 is loose. It does fire on 100% of those steps, but relative activations there range from about 0.31 to 0.69, so the input token does affect magnitude.

The residual at t=5 (L=4 recall_idx 1, about 10% of those steps fire; L=3 recall_idx 2, about 19% fire) is partly token-dependent: inputs k, q, h fire at 33-62% precision. Adding (t==5)&(L<=4)&in_tok in {k,q} gives test F1 0.906 against 0.902, a negligible gain, so this is not a meaningful systematic gap.

All other factual claims check out on test: precision 1.0 with zero false positives, the L=3 t=4 clause holds 74% of mass and almost all of the top quartile, and there is no activity on the delimiter step, at t=1-3, or at t>=6.
